clue.text: Go home and go to bed

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
to be home is to be in

explanation.surface: Someone heading home for an early night.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for retiring for the night, as in heading upstairs to sleep.

clue.text: Disquiet around 10 involved rum lot

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece, enclosing it
involved means tangled up, so the letters of rum lot are mixed

parts.note: 10 down is INDEPENDENT, abbreviated I as in political listings

explanation.surface: A rowdy group of drinkers causes unease to a neutral onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns RUM LOT into TURMOL, and 'around' wraps that round I, the usual abbreviation for an Independent politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe a state of agitation and unrest.

clue.text: More than one spoke in excellent 11

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
eleven in Roman numerals is II as two ones; the clue number is read as a figure

explanation.surface: Someone spoke up at a splendid 11 across, a party gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a reference to 11 across, but here it is just the digits, written as two Roman ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural geometric term: the spokes of a wheel run from hub to rim like lines from a centre.

clue.text: Bonk till briefly convulsing, producing a meaningful stain?

indicators.note: convulsing means writhing, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter from the word till

explanation.surface: A saucy scene that leaves behind a telltale mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens TILL to TIL; 'convulsing' mixes BONK and TIL. The definition alludes to the Rorschach test, where a blot is read for meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists' Rorschach cards show a splodge of ink the patient interprets, so the stain carries meaning.

clue.text: Informal chat, as 21 initially formed at 8 15

parts.note: 21 down is PARTY, and Con is short for the Conservative party

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A casual chat, like the gathering where a party was first set up in Bradford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent Labour Party was founded at a conference in Bradford in 1893, which is the theme. 'initially' gives F, A and B from 'formed at Bradford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial shortening of confabulation, meaning a casual conversation or natter.

clue.text: Over an hour in school to write the alphabet once

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: in places the hour inside the school

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A pupil spends over an hour at school learning to write letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, a GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient script of notches used for early Irish inscriptions, no longer in use.

clue.text: Intense dissonance amongst four voices? Not initially

indicators.note: dissonance is clashing sound, so the letters among the words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: says the opening letter of voices is not used

parts.note: taken as written, less its first letter

explanation.surface: A barbershop quartet singing out of tune makes a fierce noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' drops the V of VOICES, leaving OICES; 'dissonance amongst' mixes FOUR and OICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something fierce or extreme in strength, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Gang member in 21 dress

indicators.note: in places the dress inside the party

parts.note: 21 down is PARTY, and a band is a party of people
to rig out is to dress

explanation.surface: A gangster turns up in a party frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or robber is one of a lawless band, so a gang member fits.

clue.text: City supporter, in favour of entering cups

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that gives support

indicators.note: entering puts the favour word inside the cup sizes

parts.note: DD is a bra cup size
for means in favour of

explanation.surface: A football fan who backs the side and is into drinking cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a football fan of City, but it is underwear, and 'cups' carries on the joke with bra sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in West Yorkshire, England, where the Independent Labour Party was founded.

clue.text: Man with unkempt red hair that is 27 21 leader

parts.note: a chess man can be the king, K

indicators.note: unkempt hair is messed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dishevelled redhead who heads a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 21 is LABOUR PARTY. KEIR HARDIE founded the Independent Labour Party and was the first leader of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish trade unionist who led the parliamentary Labour group from 1906, its first leader.

clue.text: Outside 21s for us

definitions.meaning: a politician belonging to no party stands outside the parties
the newspaper that printed the puzzle speaks of itself

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the newspaper itself, so 'us' is the setter speaking for the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-aligned candidate, and the title of the newspaper carrying this crossword.

clue.text: Backing of non-professionals by very large 21

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: laic means lay, of people who are not clergy or professionals
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Amateurs supported by a huge political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is PARTY, here a gathering, not a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering, a party in the festive sense rather than the political one.

clue.text: Protest by artist in court in Cleveland?

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: in places the artist inside the court

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter stages a protest in an Ohio courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleveland' looks like the Ohio city; it is Grover Cleveland, US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland, 22nd and 24th US president, belonged to that political party, so he is an example.

clue.text: Work by old poet, such as Auden or Betjeman for starters

definitions.text: such as Auden or Betjeman for starters

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A piece written by a dead poet, like Auden or Betjeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun for a poem but is the anagram signal. The initials of Auden and Betjeman give AB, a group in the ABO system.
explanation.definitionFit: AB is one classification of human blood, so the initials make an example.

clue.text: Musical theatre round-up for agent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
rep is repertory theatre
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A spy gathers a roundup of musical theatre news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round-up' looks like one word for a summary; the hyphen splits it into a piece and the 'up' signal, which in a down clue reads the whole string from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent or spy is called an operative in espionage jargon.

clue.text: See 8
With red pants, wife was attractive

indicators.note: pants as a verb is British slang for poor, here taken as messing up the letters

explanation.surface: A wife in red trousers looked alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' reads as trousers, but is British slang for rubbish, signalling an anagram of RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to attract, as a show draws crowds; past tense matches the verb phrase.

clue.text: Rang Ted about police search?

indicators.note: about means around and astray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned Ted to ask about a hunt by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A coordinated police sweep to catch suspects, a figurative net dragged through an area.

clue.text: 10 peacekeepers before one fool retired?

indicators.note: before puts the peacekeepers ahead of what follows

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces
one is I and a fool is an ASS; having retired, the pair are pictured in BED, so I and ASS sit inside it

explanation.surface: Neutral peacekeepers are stationed ahead of an idiot who has gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' does double duty, picturing the one fool tucked up in bed: it gives the container and signals the placing, so the three words act as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Independent here means impartial, not leaning to any side.

clue.text: Fashionable soft drink for king's daughter

parts.note: in means fashionable
Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange

explanation.surface: A trendy soft drink is chosen for a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish and Portuguese royal title for a princess born to the monarch.

clue.text: Nancy's in love with roué — man out to charm

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A French woman falls for a rake who is out to charm her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy's in love' is a second wordplay: French (as spoken in Nancy) for in love is EN AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or make someone fall for you; a synonym verb.

clue.text: Gall shown by Greek character, cycling during rock band's comeback

indicators.note: during puts the cycled letters within the band
comeback means returning, so the band's name is read backwards

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra

indicators.note: cycling moves the final letter round to the front

parts.note: kappa is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek cyclist shows nerve at a rock group's reunion tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the Greek letter's final A to its front, and 'comeback' turns the band's initials round to OLE; 'during' sets the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A round growth on oak trees caused by wasp larvae, one kind of plant gall.

clue.text: Split variable in function

parts.note: to part is to split
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A maths student splits a variable within a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks mathematical beside 'variable', but it is a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal social gathering, a celebration.

clue.text: Great 25, one joining 10 27 21?

parts.note: fab is slang for great
25 across is SCOT, and Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A splendid Scotsman signs up to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 27 21 is Independent Labour Party; the Fabian Society was among Labour's founding bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Fabian Society, a socialist group, were among those linked to early Labour politics.

clue.text: Bossa nova singer

indicators.note: nova is Portuguese and Latin for new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist performs bossa nova, the Brazilian musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bossa nova' reads as the dance style; 'nova', meaning new, rearranges BOSSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass voice, the lowest male register, from the Italian name for that singer.

clue.text: Something small and negative, demanding a new clue — or not, perhaps

parts.note: a tip is a clue or hint

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A grumpy solver insists on a different clue, or maybe doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR NOT into ROTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle carrying negative charge, the antimatter counterpart of a positive one.

clue.text: 9, say, a good person holding firm

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the saint wraps around the firm

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good person
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A kindly person keeps a firm grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is KEIR HARDIE, born in Lanarkshire, so he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Hardie was born in Scotland, so a native of that country is what he exemplifies.

clue.text: Drawn to the old method of patterning textiles

parts.note: a drawn game is tied
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Someone attracted to a traditional craft of decorating cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn to' suggests attraction; it is a tied match, and 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyeing technique where fabric is knotted or bound so colour forms patterns.

clue.text: End of term 21?

definitions.meaning: the conclusion of a pregnancy carried to term is childbirth
21 is PARTY, and this is a political party by example

explanation.walkthrough: 'term' suggests a school term or politics; it is the full term of pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Childbirth is called by this word, and it is also the name of a major UK political party.
